title: Recombinant protein expression in E. coli BL21(DE3) with IPTG induction (cold overnight)
summary: Grow a kanamycin-selected BL21(DE3) culture to mid-log, induce with IPTG at reduced temperature, and harvest cells the next day. Parameters are taken from the Methods of a crystallography paper (zinc-binding CRBNmidi construct) and are a worked example, not a universal recipe.

steps.text: Inoculate lysogeny broth containing kanamycin (50 ug/mL) with the BL21(DE3) transformant carrying the expression plasmid.
Shake the culture at 37 C (temperature assumed, not stated in the paper) until the optical density at 600 nm reaches about 0.8.

duration_s.note: Growth time to OD600 0.8 is not stated; 2-4 h typical, 3 h midpoint assumed.

steps.text: Cool the flask, then induce with 0.5 mM IPTG; for this zinc-binding target also add 50 uM ZnCl2.
Continue shaking overnight at 18 C to favour soluble protein.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation (speed and time not given in the source; typically a few thousand x g for 15 min) and store or lyse immediately.

duration_s.note: Typical bench value, not from the source.

safety: Wear gloves and lab coat; treat recombinant E. coli as biosafety level 1 and decontaminate cultures and consumables before disposal.
notes: Source reports OD600 0.8, 0.5 mM IPTG, 18 C overnight, and kanamycin 50 ug/mL. Pre-induction temperature, harvest spin and all durations are assumptions flagged per step. Transformation step of the pipeline is not covered by this source.
